(a) the basic characteristics of E2 metabolism in brain are quite similar in male and female rats and (b) the relationship between cytosol and nuclear E2 binding may differ in brain from that observed in other tissues.

(1) in the brain and pituitary of the adult rat, E2 binding sites are present in both the cytoplasm and the cell nucleus, (2) E2 is metabolized in brain and pituitaries to 2-hydroxyestradiol (2-OHE2) and 16alpha-hydroxyestrone (16alpha-OHE1) in the cytosol and to 2-OHE2 in the nucleus, (3) E2 binding
the kinetics of E2 metabolism, E2 retention in cytosol and in cell nuclei are quite similar in the brains of male and female rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the binding of estrogen in the brain of the rat and the possible role of the estrogen in the regulation of brain functions.
the metabolism and binding of estrogen in brain tissue.
the study of the binding of the steroid hormone estradiol to specific cytoplasmic receptor proteins in the central nervous system of female rats.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the brain of the GX-ADX rat, E2 binding sites and E2 metabolism appear to be similar in male and female animals, but that the relationship between cytosol and cell nuclear estrogen-binding may be different in neural tissues from that observed in other tissues.
, with respect to E2 binding, the male brain appears to be quite similar to the female brain.
the cytoplasmic E2 binding system of the rat brain is not a simple reflection of the nuclear system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the basic properties of estrogen metabolism in the brain are similar in males and females, and that these properties are similar to those observed in other target tissues.
the cytoplasmic binding sites in the brain are replenished much faster than those of the cell nucleus.
estrogen receptors in the brain are similar in male and female rats and that the sex differences in the brain are not related to differences in estrogen binding.
